text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Prices of tractors made at Tractorul SA in Brasov went up by 25 percent.
- Strike of Bulgarian customs officers brought traffic to a halt at border crossings between Romania and Bulgaria.
- Shock therapy is the only solution for Romania to get out of the present economic crisis, the paper quotes Horia Rusu, a leader of Liberal Party '93, as saying.
- Government delays tender for 15 prospective oil blocks as it still has to appoint a new boss at the National Agency for Mineral Resources, the paper says.
- Renel RA electricity authority has to cash 1.72 trillion lei from bad debtors.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania's Petrolexportimport and Chase Manhattan signed in London an accord for a $200 million credit, the paper says.
ADEVARUL
- The government's social protection programme will focus mainly on children, elderly farmers and unemployed people. Tens of loss-making companies will be closed, the paper says.
- Real competition is the only solution for Romania's economy to recover and to fight inflation, the paper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Leaders of centrist parties in the ruling coalition vowed to support the government's economic reform programme, the paper says.
General:
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Prosecutors started to investigate the role allegedly played by miners' trade union leader Ilie Torsan in the 1991 riots which ousted ex-prime minister Petre Roman from office.
- Television stations are allowed to broadcast X-rated movies only after midnight, according to a decision by the National Broadcasting Council.
ADEVARUL
- Romania's integration into NATO is not necessarilly linked to the signing of a basic treaty with Ukraine, former foreign minister Teodor Melescanu is quoted as saying.
-- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264 ($=5,974 lei)
